title: ALEF commercial image orders
status: orders only; nothing here is drawn, wired, merged or deployed
houseStyle:
You are drawing a matching set of pictures for ALEF, a Hebrew-learning app for adults.
Keep the look of the app's existing pictures: the golden olive tree, the green-and-gold medallions,
and the characters Ari, Noa and Rimon exactly as on the attached sheets.

HOUSE STYLE ("Tree"): flat vector illustration, thick rounded charcoal outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills,
no gradients, no gloss, no photo-realism, no 3D render, gentle light from the upper left.
Every subject is centred with a 10% margin unless the row says otherwise.

PALETTE: deep green #1E4634, darkest green #16301C, olive #6B7F3A, warm gold #D9A441,
light gold #E9C46A, paper cream #F6F1E7, warm white #FFFAF0, pomegranate red #B0373B (small accents only).
Navy #1F3A5F only where a character already wears it (Ari's T-shirt, Rimon's scarf). No other colours.

CHARACTERS (never redesign them):
- Ari: a friendly Israeli man around 35, short dark curly hair, trimmed beard, warm brown skin,
  navy T-shirt, simple silver chain; no kippah unless the row says "synagogue look".
- Noa: a friendly Israeli woman around 32, shoulder-length wavy dark hair, olive skin,
  terracotta blouse, small gold hoop earrings.
- Rimon: a round red pomegranate mascot with the pomegranate's own small gold crown on top,
  a navy scarf, rosy cheeks, a simple smile, short stick arms and legs.

RULES FOR EVERY PICTURE
- No text of any kind: no letters in any alphabet, no numbers, no words in speech bubbles,
  no captions, no logos, no pseudo-Hebrew. Books, prayer books, cards, signs, maps and screens
  are closed, blank, or show plain lines only. Hebrew is added later by the app as real type.
- Everyday modest clothing. No depiction of God. No open Torah scroll. No Temple objects.
- Draw exactly one picture per row, at the size the row gives. No border or frame unless the row asks.
- When a row says "transparent": a PNG with a transparent background. If transparency is not
  available, use one flat solid magenta #FF00FF background with no shadow, and no magenta in the subject.

groups.title: App Icon Set
groups.why: Seen before anything else: the home screen, the install prompt, the browser tab, notifications and both store listings. Today's icon is navy (#1F3A5F) and cream from the old palette, so it clashes with the green-and-gold app. Its letter is an SVG `<text>` element in FreeSerif or DejaVu, so each device draws the alef in whatever font it has, and its PNGs have rounded corners baked in, while store guides say to upload a full square because Google Play applies its own rounded mask.
groups.plan: The alef is never generated. It is the real alef from Frank Ruhl Libre Black (already in the repo, SIL OFL), outlined to a vector path: `docs/images/orders/alef-mark-v2.svg`. A vector-only version already works and is the fallback (`docs/images/orders/icon-concept-preview.png`: old icon, new icon, new maskable, then 96/64/48/32 px). The one generated picture is a background plate that adds depth at large sizes (store 1024, Play 512, the 180 touch icon). Compare the plate version with the plain vector version at 48 px and at 1024 px and keep whichever reads better; the small sizes (192 and under, favicons) use the plain vector version either way.
groups.wiring: After John approves the look: manifest.webmanifest `icons` point at assets/icons/v2 (any 192 and 512, maskable 192 and 512, monochrome 512); index.html `rel=icon` -> assets/icons/v2/icon.svg and `rel=apple-touch-icon` -> assets/icons/v2/apple-touch-icon-180.png; notify.js `badge` -> assets/icons/v2/notify-badge-96.png. FIRST-INSTALL BUDGET: the install is 4,129,564 bytes today, 12,311 bytes under the 3.95 MiB target, and the six current icon files are precached (33,884 bytes). New PNGs in assets/icons/v2 would be precached too, so in the same commit keep only icon.svg installed up front and list the v2 PNGs as on-demand in tools/build-precache.mjs (the browser fetches manifest icons itself at install), then retire the old six from the precache list. Old files stay in git until John says otherwise.

groups.title: Store Screenshots and Install-Dialog Screenshots
groups.why: The screenshots sell the app on both store pages and in Chrome's install dialog, which is live today. The current manifest screenshots (assets/screens, 390x844 and 1280x800) show the earlier navy design and a "no recordings exist yet" banner, with no captions and no characters.
groups.plan: Six screenshot stories, each = real app screen in a simple phone frame + a short caption + one character cut-out. Only the cut-outs and one background pattern are generated; captions are real type added by the build script (Heebo 800, warm white #FFFAF0 on the green background). Captions reuse copy the app already shows; John approves the wording.
groups.wiring: manifest.webmanifest `screenshots`: replace the eight current entries with the v2 narrow (5) and wide (3) files, each with `form_factor` and a `label` that repeats the caption. assets/screens/ is already on-demand in the precache rules, so no install-size cost. The store/ folder is outside src, assets and data, so it is never precached; it only holds uploads for the two stores.
groups.compositeRecipe: Capture each screen in Chrome at 440x956 CSS px, device scale 3 (that is exactly 1320x2868), light theme, the Rimon greeting bubble closed. Composite for 1320x2868: background flat #1E4634 at the top fading to #16301C at the bottom, PATTERN_v2_olive tiled at 8% strength; caption centred, top 150 to 560 px, Heebo 800 at 96 px, warm white #FFFAF0, at most two lines, a 120x8 px gold #D9A441 rule under it; phone frame = rounded rectangle 1000x2170 px at x 160, y 640, radius 120, 18 px #0F2416 bezel, the capture scaled into it; the story's cut-out 720 px tall, overlapping a lower corner of the frame by about 120 px. Google Play and the narrow manifest set use the same layout at 1080x1920 (scale 0.818, phone frame shortened to fit). iPad: same layout at 2064x2752 with an iPad-shaped frame.

groups.title: Onboarding (First Run)
groups.why: Every new learner sees these four steps (src/onboarding/firstrun.view.js: letters, congregation, minutes, plan). Today they are text and radio buttons only, and the Welcome card has no picture. A friendly picture per step is the standard in top learning apps and makes the first two minutes feel guided.
groups.plan: One wide banner for the Welcome card and one round spot picture per step, shown at about 152 px in a circle above the step heading.
groups.wiring: firstrun.view.js: render the banner above the h1 and one decorative image (alt="", 152 px circle, loading=lazy) above each step's h2, through the same image resolver the other views use (generated-manifest ids). Images are under assets/img/gen, which is runtime-cached, so no install-size cost; a missing or unapproved image simply draws nothing.

groups.why: The 25 milestone medallions are drawn and approved. Six awards still have no art, so the gallery falls back to a plain line glyph: the two practice badges, the Beginner checklist, and the three mastery finish slots (src/awards/eligibility.js).
groups.plan: Same recipe as the approved set, so they sit in the grid without a seam. The gallery already looks up BADGE_<award id>, so these names wire themselves once approved. Optional: 1600x1600 if your tool offers it, to match the existing sources.
groups.wiring: None for the six new ones: src/awards/gallery.view.js already looks up BADGE_<id> and shows it once approved.

groups.why: Brain Lab is ten drills on a text-only page (src/lab/lab.core.js GAMES). A header picture and one token per drill make the workout list scannable at a glance, the way fitness-style brain apps look.
groups.plan: One wide header and ten round tokens, shown at 56 px beside each drill name. A cover, an in-game picture and a results picture for every drill are ordered in [BRAIN-LAB-ORDERS-2026-11-09.md](BRAIN-LAB-ORDERS-2026-11-09.md).
groups.wiring: src/lab/lab.view.js: the header above the h1 and each token (alt="", 56 px) at the start of its drill row; ids LAB_v2_<game id> match GAMES ids.

groups.why: The Learn page asks learners to pick "Read the prayer book" or "Speak in Israel" with two plain pill buttons (src/curriculum/learn.view.js). A cover picture per track makes the choice clear at a glance.
groups.plan: Two wide covers, shown cropped to 2:1 above each track.
groups.wiring: learn.view.js: show the chosen track's cover (alt="", 2:1 crop, loading=lazy) above its lesson list.

images.style: House style. No symbols or writing anywhere.

notOrdered.why: Ari and Noa (14 approved poses), Rimon (MASCOT_rimon and the frame sheets in assets/img/rimon) already exist. Every order above reuses them.
HERO_home_tree and HERO_olive_harvest_astral already exist and are kept. They are painterly while the rest is flat; that mix is left as is.
GAME_minute_one_celebration, GAME_letter_rush, GAME_tradition_detective and other GAME_ art are on the open games-first-words branches; nothing here repeats them.
SHARE_bg_01 to 10 stay pending: the app has no share button yet (no navigator.share in src), so they would not show anywhere.
None: the award rules have no Brain Lab award, and inventing one is a product decision for John.

alsoWithoutNewArt: Badge crops: re-crop five medallions (see rank 8). No new art.
Awards page: about 49,000 px tall on a phone, mostly explanation. Folding the rules text into one "How awards work" section would let the medallion grid lead. Copy and layout only.
Badge size: the gallery draws medallions at 64 px (.aw-badge-art). 88 px makes the art read as a reward. CSS only.
